Question B-006-008-004.

Why the correct answer is right: Radio waves in free space travel at the speed of light, approximately 300 000 kilometres per second.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "200 000 kilometres per second": This is about 0.67 times 300 000 km/s, resembling a coax velocity-factor value, but the question asks for propagation in free space.
- sourceIndex 2: "150 000 kilometres per second": This is half of the correct free-space speed, 300 000 / 2 = 150 000 km/s; half-wavelength arithmetic should not be applied to wave speed.
- sourceIndex 3: "186 000 kilometres per second": This is the speed of light expressed in miles per second; 186 000 miles/s is about 300 000 km/s, so labelling 186 000 as kilometres per second uses the wrong unit.
